elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 17(d): "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall ..." — covers both expiry and termination, on any ground.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: (1) "at Sparkling's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months"; the request condition is not limited to anticipated expiry, so it applies after any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates" — Vendor's then-current rates expressly stated.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: (2) "within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in Garman's possession or control" — the 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: (3) "after such return, delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Sparkling" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted opening words: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six-month assistance window exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Return of all of Sparkling's data within thirty calendar days of expiry or termination in a machine-readable format satisfies the export requirement.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: existing Sections 17(b), 17(c), 16 and 18 only require Sparkling to return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and impose no exit assistance or data-return duty on Garman.
All six preferred elements are carried by the single inserted Section 17(d); no element is left to the margin comment or to an undefined trigger.

Minimality holds: the redline is one concise inserted paragraph in the termination section, with no deletion or paraphrase of retained language (17(b), the default/perpetual-licence sentence and the survival provision are untouched) and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense wording or added remedies.

Intent preserved: the existing survival clause uses "include but are not limited to," so new 17(d) survives without needing amendment; "all of Sparkling's data in Garman's possession or control" is descriptive rather than an undefined defined term, so no dangling reference is created, and the drafter correctly avoided importing a non-existent "Customer Data" definition.
